criteria.text: Running `pdd test place-order` for the first time with a signed-in `gh` token calls `gh auth token` once and `gh api user` once, saves login `"octo"`, user ID `"4242"` and the token's SHA-256 digest in private state without saving the raw token, and exits with code 0.

Polling a saved batch with `pdd test --read BATCH --json` when the `gh` token matches the saved SHA-256 digest calls `gh auth token` once and `gh api user` 0 times, and exits with code 0 even when GitHub's REST rate limit is exhausted; running `pdd lint`, `pdd test`, `pdd simulate` and `pdd mcp` Try commands with that same token also calls `gh api user` 0 times.

After switching to another GitHub account whose `gh` token has a different SHA-256 digest, running `pdd test --read BATCH` for `"octo"`'s saved batch calls `gh api user` once, updates the saved login for the active token, prints `"These runs belong to octo. Run: gh auth switch -u octo"` to stderr and exits with code 5.

When `gh auth token` fails or returns blank while a saved login file exists, `pdd test --read BATCH` calls `gh api user` 0 times, prints `"Run gh auth login"` to stderr and exits with code 5; when no matching saved login exists and `gh api user` fails, `pdd` prints `"pdd could not read your GitHub login (gh api user: <reason>). Run gh auth status."` to stderr and exits with code 5.

When the PDD interpreter answers HTTP 401 during a command that used the saved login, `pdd` clears the saved login, refreshes `gh auth token` and `gh api user` once, retries the request once when the owner still matches, and if the interpreter still answers HTTP 401 prints `"The PDD interpreter did not accept your GitHub login (HTTP 401). Run gh auth login, then run the command again."` to stderr and exits with code 5.

setup.isolation: Fresh temporary Git repository copied from test/fixtures/harbor; external PDD_STATE_DIR per case; deterministic injected clock, UUIDs, gh port and local HTTP fakeRuntime. No live GitHub or interpreter calls.

state_cache_schema.token_sha256: 64-character lowercase hex SHA-256 of trimmed gh auth token

security_invariants.atomic_write: same-directory temporary file + rename; no leftover temp files

cases.given: Empty external PDD_STATE_DIR; gh auth token returns TOKEN_OCTO and gh api user returns 'octo 4242'.

Batch saved by octo from cold-cache-first-run with terminal check receipts on disk and matching github-user.json; gh api user stub fails with status 1 and stderr 'gh: API rate limit exceeded (HTTP 403)'.
Valid github-user.json for TOKEN_OCTO ('octo', '4242') in PDD_STATE_DIR; gh auth token returns TOKEN_OCTO and gh api user fails if called.
Saved batch and open Try owned by 'octo' ('4242') with github-user.json for TOKEN_OCTO; operator switches GitHub account so gh auth token returns TOKEN_MALLORY and gh api user returns 'mallory 777'.
commands: pdd simulate place-order --page --no-open --no-wait (with explicit --max-calls 400 or connected reuse)

cases.given: Valid github-user.json for 'octo' exists on disk; subcase A: gh binary missing (ENOENT); subcase B: gh auth token exits 1 or prints empty stdout.

expected.enoent_stderr_contains: Install the GitHub CLI, then run gh auth login

cases.given: github-user.json contains truncated JSON ('{bad'), missing token_sha256, whitespace/empty login, or non-positive user_id ('0' or 'abc'); gh auth token returns TOKEN_OCTO and gh api user returns 'octo 4242'.

Subcase A: sign-in came from github-user.json, first runtime HTTP call returns 401, fresh gh auth token + gh api user returns rotated TOKEN_OCTO_2 for 'octo 4242', and single retry returns 200. Subcase B: fresh lookup after 401 returns 'mallory 777' on octo's saved batch/Try. Subcase C: single retry after refresh also returns 401. Subcase D: initial sign-in was cold-cache (already called gh api user fresh in this command) and runtime returns 401.

expected.subcase_c_stderr_contains: The PDD interpreter did not accept your GitHub login (HTTP 401). Run gh auth login, then run the command again.

Subcase B: forced refresh while valid matching-token github-user.json exists and gh api user fails with GitHub rate limit during saved local batch --read vs. remote check/post-401 refresh.
